#3477. Palm Beach Co-Pilot Nathalia's Flight Instructor Says She Was 'Born to Fly'

Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was a "natural-born pilot" ... according to one of the first instructors who taught her, who's now paying tribute to the young co-pilot killed in the tragic Palm Beach plane crash.

Chris Kirk, who says he was one of Nathalia's first instructors and mentors, took to social media to defend her flying abilities ... making it clear she wasn't just another pilot looking to cash in on an airline career.

Kirk said he'd been teaching for 40 years and she was "without a doubt the most naturally gifted pilot I have ever taught" ... adding, Nathalia routinely impressed examiners during her check rides, saying "that young lady was born to fly!"

The instructor also recalled Nathalia completing her Learjet type rating with fewer than 1,100 flight hours under her belt. He says she absolutely aced the pilot-in-command certification, with the examiner thinking she'd logged closer to 5,000 hours.

And apparently, she wasn't afraid to get her hands dirty in the cockpit ... Kirk says he gave her opportunities to fly all kinds of aircraft, including tailwheel planes and the Caravan.

Kirk says Nathalia's passion for aviation was what really set her apart, taking a swipe at other pilots in training who, in his experience, were more interested in getting to the airlines and making big money rather than actually loving the job.

As we previously reported ... Nathalia was serving as co-pilot aboard a Learjet 60 traveling from Austin, Texas to the Bahamas, when it crashed in Palm Beach County ... killing all nine people aboard, including captain Jeff Gregory and family of CEO Adam Robinson.

We also reported Nathalia sent her pilot boyfriend a chilling text shortly before the November 1 crash ... telling him, "I've got turbulence, I've got ice," according to her stepfather, Thiago Corleti.

The NTSB is investigating what caused the crash. Investigators have been examining reports of icing and turbulence, along with parts of the aircraft that seemingly separated before the striking impact.

#3476. 10 Best Stephen King Books of All Time, Ranked According to Goodreads

Stephen King is the undisputed master of literary horror. No one else in the genre comes close to him in terms of quality or quality. He has penned over 60 novels and 200 short stories, continuously captivating readers with his exploration of the dark corners of the human psyche. His best works, like The Shining, It, and Misery, are not just tales of terror but profound examinations of family, addiction, and madness. In addition, they are great snapshots of late 20th-century America, particularly its small towns.

Indeed, King's talents go beyond horror, as evidenced in more dramatic stories like The Shawshank Redemption and The Green Mile. His writing is also highly visual, lending itself well to the screen. Some of the greatest movies of all time have been made based on his work. This dense, varied bibliography means he's sure to continue frightening readers for generations to come. Those looking to get started with his work could do worse than to look to his most highly-rated books on the review site Goodreads. These are King's best projects, ranked according to its users.

"And then the world exploded." King's electric debut revolves around a shy, bullied high school girl with a deeply religious and abusive mother. Her life takes a drastic turn when she discovers her telekinetic powers. After being humiliated at her prom by a cruel prank, Carrie unleashes her newfound abilities in a fit of rage, leading to a night of devastation in her small town.

The book is short (not even 200 pages) but packs an outsize punch. It's also structurally inventive, including excerpts from fictional books, newspapers, and reports, as well as contributions from various narrators. Reportedly, King grew dissatisfied with the book early on in the writing process, discarding the pages he'd written in the trash. His wife Tabitha retrieved them and insisted he continue. It's a good thing she did: Carrie was a bestseller, launching its author's career and helping to bring horror fiction into the mainstream.

"Death is a mystery, and burial is a secret." Louis Creed moves with his family to a rural town in Maine, where he discovers a nearby pet cemetery with a dark secret. When tragedy strikes and Louis's son, Gage, is killed in an accident, he learns of an ancient burial ground beyond the pet cemetery that can bring the dead back to life, but at a terrible cost. Pet Sematary features some of the oldest horror tropes around, like a character who violates the finality of death and must suffer the consequences.

However, King breathes new life into these old chestnuts and makes them chilling once more. In large part, this is because the characters are complex and believable. They feel like real people, and the reader sympathizes with them, making their ordeals all the more horrific. For these reasons, Guillermo del Toro has said it's one of the books he would most like to adapt. "As a father, I now understand it better than I ever would have, and it scares me a hundred times more," he explains.

"When the evil falls on the town, its coming seems almost preordained." 'Salem's Lot centers on Ben Mears, a writer who returns to his hometown to find inspiration for his new book. However, he soon discovers that the townspeople are falling prey to a sinister force — a centuries-old vampire named Kurt Barlow. Once again, King takes a well-worn idea — in this case, a vampire story — but reinvigorates it by relocating the action to a fresh setting: a small New England town in the mid-70s.

King has described the book as "Peyton Place meets Dracula", which is accurate. In a lesser writer's hands, this tale might have come out fangless, but 'Salem's Lot is decidedly creepy and compelling. In addition to the vampire thrills, the small-town drama is intriguing as well. The book is populated with a large cast of realistic characters, all of whom have their own struggles and secrets. This recipe translated well to the screen, resulting in a terrific miniseries adaptation. A new film version is in development as well.

"I am your number one fan." King gets a little meta with this psychological thriller in which a bestselling author, Paul Sheldon, is kidnapped by his "number one fan," Annie Wilkes, after a car accident. Annie, a former nurse with a dangerous fixation on Paul's work, forces him to write a new novel that revives her favorite character, Misery Chastain. Trapped in Annie's remote home, Paul endures physical and psychological torture as he struggles to escape her clutches.

The book is incredibly tense. The reader roots desperately for Paul to break free, only to have their hopes dashed repeatedly. King's protagonists are often authors (write what you know, and all that), but Paul might be his most vivid and likable. He's definitely a little autobiographical, too. King has said that Paul feeling chained to his Misery character was a stand-in for King feeling boxed into the horror genre. He has also said that Annie Wilkes is a metaphor for drug addiction.

"Terrible things happen in the world, and they're things no one can explain." Struggling writer and recovering alcoholic Jack Torrance takes a job as the winter caretaker of the Overlook Hotel, a remote resort with a sinister history. He brings with him his wife, Wendy, and their young son, Danny, who possesses psychic abilities. As winter sets in, the hotel's malevolent influence begins to fray Jack's sanity.

Though not quite as good as Stanley Kubrick's film version, The Shining is top-tier King, and certainly one of his scariest books. It was his third published novel and is considerably more ambitious than Carrie and 'Salem's Lot, which had preceded it. Here, he draws inspiration from Edgar Allan Poe and Shirley Jackson's The Haunting of Hill House but filters it through his distinctive perspective. The result is an intelligent ghost story that elevates character over gore or action.

"Books are a uniquely portable magic." On Writing is a hybrid book: part memoir, part guidebook for aspiring writers. Here, King shares his journey from a struggling writer to a bestselling author, providing insights into his creative process, work ethic, and the experiences that shaped his stories. It's chock-full of simple but powerful writing advice, placing it among the best works on the topic. King's description of his work habits is especially fascinating.

King wrote the book while recovering from being hit by a van, and his inner struggles are evident on the page. This was clearly a difficult project for him. However, the book is also impressive and triumphant, with King rediscovering his voice, creativity, and passion for the craft. As a result, On Writing is a moving book that can be appreciated by anyone, not just budding writers or horror fans. It's one of the strongest works the author has ever produced.

"Because the dark surrounds us, let us turn our faces to the light." 11/22/63 is a uniquely King blend of historical fiction and time travel. The novel follows Jake Epping, a high school teacher who discovers a portal to the year 1958 in the back of a diner. He sets out on a mission to prevent JFK's assassination on November 22, 1963. Soon, Epping bonds with people from the past, finding himself torn between times.

The premise is a little ridiculous, but King pulls it off, resulting in one of his most sweeping, moving novels. His recreation of the '50s and '60s is immersive, reflecting the huge amount of research he did while writing it. The characters are also well-drawn, particularly Jake's fiancée Sadie. This means that when tragedy strikes, it hits the reader even harder. Perhaps as a result, 11/22/63 was one of King's most acclaimed novels of the 2010s, with the New York Times going so far as to rank it among the top five fiction books of the year.

"We lie best when we lie to ourselves." It is a monumental work of horror that delves into the nature of fear and the power of memory. It alternates between two timelines, following a group of friends known as the Losers' Club as children in the 1950s and as adults in the 1980s. The friends are united by their encounters with a malevolent entity that takes the form of their worst fears, most often appearing as a clown named Pennywise.

King wasn't the first writer to describe a monster that takes on the form of whatever its victim fears most, but he certainly did it the most memorably. Pennywise is now an iconic villain, in his literary and cinematic forms: the shot of him peeking out from a sewer is seared into many people's brains. Beneath the frights, though, It is a smart, frustrating, overlong, controversial but undeniably imaginative work and a standout of '80s horror.

"That wasn't any act of God." Another King epic, The Stand takes place in the aftermath of a global pandemic that has wiped out most of the human population. The survivors are drawn into two factions: one led by the kind and wise Mother Abagail, and the other by the sinister and charismatic Randall Flagg. As the survivors rebuild their lives, they must prepare for an inevitable confrontation between the forces of good and evil.

This is essentially King's take on Lord of the Rings but set in a post-apocalyptic version of Las Vegas. It features bomb blasts, supernatural powers, countless characters, and the vilest of villains. Although not one of his most accessible books for newcomers, The Stand is vivid, intense, and grand in scale. The extended edition clocks in at well over 1000 pages. It's probably the most ambitious thing King has ever done. Critics responded; both Time magazine and the BBC have ranked The Stand among the best books of all time.

"Sometimes there is absolutely no difference at all between salvation and damnation." King's highest-rated book on Goodreads is less of a horror and more of a supernatural drama. The Green Mile takes place in the 1930s at Cold Mountain Penitentiary's death row. The story is narrated by Paul Edgecombe, a former prison guard who recounts his experiences with John Coffey, a giant of a man convicted of murdering two young girls. Despite his imposing appearance, Coffey possesses an extraordinary gift: the ability to heal others and absorb their suffering.

The death row setting is unique and memorable, and it's a great vehicle for King to explore issues of morality and justice. The Green Mile covers a lot of ground, pivoting from sweet and poignant to violent and horrifying. Like King's story Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption, it was adapted into an excellent film by director Frank Darabont. It's a great example of King's range and thoughtful handling of incendiary subject matter.

#3475. This 140W power station might be the ultimate charger for Apple users [Video]

I have tested and used countless charging stations over the years, and while many of them get the job done, I feel like there is always some sort of compromise. Whether it’s not enough power, lack of a certain port that I need, or slow wireless charging, I have yet to find one that truly checks every box for me. But over the last month, I have been using CUKTECH’s new 140W Powerstation, and it has nailed everything. It is a six-in-one desktop charger with a built-in retractable cable, magnetic wireless charging, and a dedicated diagnostic display, all in an aesthetic, compact package. Here is everything you need to know and why I think it’s worth considering.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video to see this CUKTECH 15 PowerStation in action!

At its core, the CUKTECH 15 PowerStation is a 140W GaN charger. It can charge one device at the full 140W, meaning it can charge your 16-in MacBook Pro PROLED XDR at max speed, or it can divvy up that power to charge up to six devices at once. It also offers a great combination of ports, a built-in cable, and multiple wireless charging options. You get:

Of course, the biggest selling point is the versatility of it all. You can charge your MacBook Pro with the main USB-C port, charge your iPad with the built-in cable, place your iPhone on the MagSafe charger, and place your AirPods on the wireless charging pad. After all of that, there are still more ports for other accessories that I use daily.

Do keep in mind that the 140W output is the total output, so if more devices are added, that output is shared across all the connected devices.

I am someone who is constantly switching between so many Apple devices. I switch between my iPad Pro and MacBook Pro all the time, and now that it is techtember, I am testing multiple iPhones at the same time, so I need to make sure all of my devices are charged up for when I need them. Not only that, but I also need a USB-A port for my camera battery charging station. So having a centralized hub to charge all of my devices is a MUST in my desk setup. So what immediately stands out to me about the CUKTECH 15 is how much functionality they were able to pack into this relatively compact charging station.

I am a huge fan of built-in retractable cables; they eliminate the need to remember to carry a USB-C cable, so you know you can charge at least one device. Then you add in the wireless magnetic charging stand that supports the new iPhone Duo and StandBy Mode, all while keeping the iPhone upright and visible. Also, when you set up that magnetic charging pad in the upright position, it reveals an AirPods Pro charger. The design is so well thought out.

The cherry on top of it all is the display. I love being able to see how fast something is charging. It allows me to see whether products meet their charging speed standards and how different devices are affected by their charge levels. CUKTECH was also smart to still include one USB-A port. Lots of companies have decided to omit that port because it is an old standard, but there are still plenty of older and wacky tech that uses USB-A, so the inclusion is appreciated. The only thing missing is a dedicated Apple Watch charger, but I just plug in my own when I need it.

The CUKTECH 15 140W Charging Station is available today on Amazon for $149. It has been out in Europe for a little while, but now it has finally made it to the US!

There are plenty of charging stations on the market, but CUKTECH’s 140W power station is the first to check off all the boxes for me. It’s compact, looks great, has all the ports and charging methods I need, and features a beautiful TFT display that lets me know things are charging as they should. If you use multiple devices throughout the day and need them charged at all times, this is worth considering.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Each school can do what it wants when it comes to restricting or banning AI. However, a new report from The New York Times report found that schools that completely ban AI will also lose access to Google Search, one of the most ubiquitous tools on the internet for finding, well, anything.

"Search and A.I. are deeply integrated," said Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google. He also explained that students "will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available."

Getting through college without access to Google sounds difficult, since almost everyone goes there when they need to learn something. Sure, Google alternatives exist, but for most people, an online search is still called "Googling."

As you might expect, Google's stance has drawn pushback. Lina Khan, former chair of the FTC, said to the NYT that Google is using its “search monopoly to coerce schools” into adopting its AI.

Obviously, Google is justifying this move by saying that AI is an integrated part of search as it stands now. And that might be true, but we had many, many years of Google Search without AI, so it's certainly possible to find content on the web without it.

"This latest move shows it remains unchastened. As the public increasingly pushes back against the use of AI in schools," Khan added. "Google is making clear it will punish those who don’t fall in line."

Two options for search inside school-issued accounts will launch in early 2027.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

The first option will be search with AI overviews and AI chats, similar to the experience we use every day. The other will be search with Guided Learning, the student feature within Google’s Gemini chatbot. This feature is meant to guide students step-by-step without just giving them the answers. It is supposed to offer an experience similar to one-on-one tutoring.

Either way, we know it's possible to use search without AI, and if Google really wanted to, it could almost certainly allow schools to keep using its search engine without AI. We did it for years.

Will Google stick to its guns here, or will the company back down if there's enough backlash? After all, Google makes a lot of its money from search ads, and if It suddenly lost millions of students, that could hurt the bottom line over time.

Amazon currently has the 32-inch Samsung Odyssey OLED G8 (G80SH) for $999.99, down from $1,299.99, and price trackers show that this is its lowest price so far. This is the newer 4K OLED model, not Samsung’s similarly named G80HS, which is a 6K IPS variant, and it makes the most sense for someone who wants one screen for both high-end gaming and everyday desktop use without moving to a larger ultrawide.

Its 4K QD-OLED panel runs at 240Hz, which gives the G80SH enough speed for competitive shooters and racing games while still keeping slower, more cinematic games looking sharp. You will need a powerful PC to get anywhere close to 4K at 240Hz, but the monitor is at least equipped for newer graphics hardware with DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1. It also has USB-C with up to 98W of power delivery, so if this monitor doubles as a work setup, a compatible laptop can send video and charge over the same cable instead of adding another wire to your desk. FreeSync Premium Pro and G-SYNC compatibility should also help keep tearing under control, though OLED monitors can still show visible VRR flicker in darker scenes when frame pacing is inconsistent.

The bigger visual difference, though, shows up in darker games and HDR content, where blacks stay properly black and bright effects stand out without the blooming you often see on LCD monitors. That said, QD-OLED does have its own drawbacks, since blacks can take on a purplish tint in a brightly lit room, while burn-in remains a long-term concern—though Samsung does include active cooling and several screen-protection features to reduce uneven wear and says burn-in from normal use is covered under warranty. If you mostly play at lower frame rates or do not care much about OLED contrast, this is probably more monitor than you need, but for someone with the graphics hardware to take advantage of 4K at 240Hz, this discount makes the G80SH much easier to justify.

‘A Dog’s Perfect Christmas’ is cozy but no Christmas classic

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Netflix’s holiday movie slate for 2026 begins its rollout this week, starting with “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas,” a streaming original that so rigidly sticks to the genre conventions that it is as predictable as unwrapping a Christmas present from that one relative who always gets you an Axe body spray gift set. Within seconds, you know exactly what you’re getting.

All the trappings of a family-focused festive-themed comedy-drama are here. By the end, everything is wrapped up in a neat bow, all to send viewers into the credits with a warm fuzzy feeling. It’s a safe holiday movie created in a tinsel-laden laboratory, where artistic merit is not the end goal. Instead, the objective is to create a product palatable for all ages.

But if “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” proves anything, it’s that throwing a couple of cute canine companions into the mix can make even a Christmas movie this flavorless at least tolerable. Which isn’t to say it has any original musings on the special connection between household pets and their owners. It doesn’t even break from the weary formula established in other dog movies like “A Dog’s Purpose” and “A Dog’s Journey.”

However, the dogs were lovable enough to thaw out even my cynical soul. It might not be a future Christmas classic — the likes of “It’s A Wonderful Life” and “Elf” will not fear their place in any family’s annual seasonal watchlist being pinched by this new Netflix movie — but dog lovers everywhere will probably find this film cozy enough to watch, if only once.

Based on the novel by W. Bruce Cameron, author of “A Dog’s Purpose,” this movie focuses on the Goss family. Their holiday festivities are already off to a rocky start, with grandpa Sander (Dennis Quaid) grieving the loss of his wife two years prior, husband Hunter (Milo Ventimiglia) putting work first, and mother Juliana (Kathleen Rose Perkins) struggling to find common ground with her moody teenage daughter, Ello (Brooke Lena Johnson).

Things take a further turn when a medical emergency throws the family into turmoil and threatens to bring a swift end to any lingering holiday cheer. It’s up to the Goss' wise old dog, a basset hound named Winstead (voiced by Thomas Haden Church), and an energetic new arrival, a Corgi puppy named Ruby (Sadie Hatch), to bring the humans back together.

I really cannot overstate just how generic “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” is. All its narrative beats have been seen in countless other holiday movies, and it has no desire to rework the genre trappings. But whether you demand, or particularly look for, originality in your holiday watchlist is a matter of personal preference. If you want a cozy family comedy, it’s a suitable way to spend 100 minutes, and it'll probably make for great background noise while putting up your own seasonal decorations, if that's your thing.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

It’s been suggested that Netflix has a mandate that its movies need to reiterate key plot points for viewers only half-watching, and while the streamer denies this, 'A Dog’s Perfect Christmas' is evidence to the contrary.

Another notable area where “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” comes up short is in its insistence on over-explaining. It’s been suggested that Netflix has a mandate that its movies need to reiterate key plot points for viewers only half-watching, and while the streamer denies this, “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” is evidence to the contrary. Characters often speak unnaturally, regurgitating facts as if they know a third party is watching their holiday season unfold and might need a reminder (or three) to follow along.

But even if “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” will no doubt be forgotten long before you take down your tree and household decorations for another year, in the moment, it’s by no means offensively bad. It’s just bland. But above all, the two dogs at the heart of the holiday crowd-pleaser are very cute and given enough screen time to make their presence felt.

“A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” celebrates family, especially these four-legged members of our homes who are just as important to the unit as any human. That’s a message that dog owners everywhere will relate to, and it gives this Netflix movie a crowd-pleasing quality. I guess it really does prove that the inclusion of a dog (or two) can make anything watchable.

#3468. 10 of the Most Iconic Patrick Stewart Roles Beyond Captain Picard

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

Sir Patrick Stewart, an actor equally at home onstage at the Royal Shakespeare Company and on the bridge of the Starship Enterprise, has died at the age of 86. Unexpectedly for most of us, in part because he kept his final illness private, but more so because it once seemed as though nothing could fell the man who looms so large in our cultural consciousness.

The thoughtful, erudite performer who had a troubled childhood in working-class Yorkshire; the committed socialist who was eventually knighted by Queen Elizabeth; the advocate who put his money and his considerable voice toward the fights for LGBTQ+ acceptance and animal welfare and against domestic violence, his presence and performances meant the world (the galaxy, even) to myself and so many others. But those who knew him personally can offer better tributes; perhaps it's best left to Shakespeare's Player King, performed by Stewart himself opposite David Warner's Hamlet back in 1965:

Where joy most revels, grief doth most lament;Grief joys, joy grieves, on slender accident.

Much of Stewart's finest work was on the stage; other performances remain rather shockingly hard to come by (whither I, Claudius?). Nonetheless, he left a true legacy behind him, well beyond Captain Picard and Professor X. Here are 10 of his most iconic other roles.

A goofy, feel-good gay rom-com with the HIV/AIDS crisis still very much in the foreground, Jeffrey was a near-impossibility in the mid-1990s: a movie that neither villainized its queers nor treated them as pitiable martyrs. Steven Weber and Michael T. Weiss are the leads, joined by a cast that includes Christine Baranski, Victor Garber, Nathan Lane, Olympia Dukakis, and Sigourney Weaver but, for all those names, Stewart is the undeniable standout as Sterling, the irrepressible gay best friend: a swishing, mincing, sassy, high-camp character who steals every scene without ever becoming a caricature. He's the leader of the "Pink Panthers," a squad of queers who defend locals from gay bashers, and that is the key to the character's power: He's as gay as they come, but not ashamed and not even a little weak. This movie, and the presence of Captain Picard himself in it, might have saved my life back in 1995. Stream Jeffrey on Prime Video, Tubi, and The Roku Channel.

A sprawling, epic, and appropriately lusty take on the King Arthur stories from John Boorman, Excalibur is a mixed bag full of stunning visuals and iconic moments that never quite coalesce into something entirely coherent. Standing out among the film's many characters, Stewart is entirely memorable as Leodegrance, the boisterous, boorish, but ultimately faithful father of Guenevere who is among the first to pledge his loyalty to Arthur. Rent Excalibur from Prime Video.

Darcy Banker is erudite and intellectual, in his way, and even capable of charm, but otherwise has no redeeming qualities whatsoever. It's bad enough for the punk band Ain’t Rights that they've booked a last-minute gig at an Oregon bar without realizing that it's a haven for white supremacists. It's even worse when they witness a murder and become trapped in the title's green room, with Stewart as the lead skinhead. He's quite simply one of the all-time great (meaning absolutely terrifying) villains in this thriller that's pretty much a horror movie. Stream Green Room on Netflix.

Patrick Stewart's role as Professor Xavier in the X-Men is almost as pop-culture iconic as that of Captain Picard, spanning 26 years and nine movies, including the forthcoming Avengers: Doomsday. In most of those, he looks like he's having an awful lot of fun, but he gives his finest performance in the role in this elegaic installment, playing a dying Professor in profound cognitive decline, his dream in tatters and his bravado worn down to prickly dependence. We rarely get to see our superheroes at the ends of their days, and there's a lovely bravery to this depiction of the Charles' journey. Logan will likely be the toughest of his films to rewatch in the coming days. Stream Logan on Disney+.

This stagey television movie isn't the most sumptuous of the many filmed versions of the Dickens story, but you won't be surprised to learn that there are few better portrayals of Ebenezer Scrooge. It's rather a shame that Patrick Stewart didn't do more Dickens adaptations, since his booming voice and ability to play thoroughly heightened characters without ever resorting to caricature is as valuable as in Shakespeare. Rent A Christmas Carol from Prime Video.

Famously referred to as that "unknown British Shakespearean actor" when starting out on Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stewart was an associate of the Royal Shakespeare Company for twenty years before his most famous role came along. As is the way of live theater, much of his career lives on as an essential link in the chain of Shakespeare performances in the twentieth century...but not in a way that we can conveniently stream. We do, however, have this impressively mounted modern-dress stage production, in which Stewart plays King Claudius with characteristic brilliance against David Tennant's melancholy prince. Buy Hamlet from Prime Video and Apple TV.

As a cinematic actor, Stewart's greatest strength was bringing humanity to larger-than-life, even operatic roles, whether they be Arthurian knights, Dickensian villains, or superheroes. That ability is an absolute necessity if one is going to have any success doing Shakespeare, as Stewart did for decades. Match is something rather different, though, and it's rather lovely to see him play something just a bit more mundane—even if the film's Tobi Powell is a choreographer with a nearly legendary reputation. Teaching at Juilliard School, with his career winding down, he's confronted with the living embodiment of the past he left behind to pursue his career. The ensuing relationships grow more complex, with the film building to a climax that's surprising and deeply devastating, made all the more so by Stewart's muted, subtle performance. Stream Match on AMC+.

This is not the greatest Mel Brooks movie, not by a long shot, but it is a great comedic performance from Patrick Stewart. He loved to recount, with self-effacing embarrassment, the story of having shouted "We are not here to have fun" at his co-workers during a rowdy day on set at Star Trek: The Next Generation. By 1993, he was clearly past any such pomposity, and clearly having fun in his cameo as King Richard, a memorably silly take on a character he might well have played with seriousness elsewhere. Rent Robin Hood: Men in Tights from Prime Video.

Stewart's first real foray into science fiction was in this big, bold, divisive, and thoroughly bonkers Frank Herbert adaptation from director David Lynch. Stewart plays troubadour and warrior Gurney Halleck, and does what he does best: bringing gravitas and believability (and it must be said, bald sexiness) to even the wildest material. Stream Dune on Tubi.

Stewart plays an aged Merlin in this rather shockingly good modern reimagining of the King Arthur legendarium. His Merlin is all wild hair and rock band T-shirts, possessed of an essential kindness that makes him a valued mentor, and one deserving of his character's poignant farewell at the film's conclusion.Stream The Kid Who Would Be King on Disney+ and Prime Video.

#3467. Three new iPad models are reportedly launching early next year, here’s what’s coming

After debuting the refreshed iPad mini with OLED this past week, Apple still has more in the pipeline for the rest of the iPad lineup in the first half of next year. That includes a new iPad Air, a new base iPad, and a new iPad Pro, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

To follow up the iPad mini refresh, Apple’s next iPad Air refresh will also gain OLED. It’ll likely stick with a 60Hz panel, and likely won’t make the switch from Touch ID to Face ID – but it’ll bring a nifty display upgrade to the iPad Air, a product that hasn’t had a major refresh since 2020.

In terms of chipset, while not confirmed, a jump from the M4 chip to the M5 chip is rather likely. It’ll also likely come with a higher price, likely around $799-899 for the base 11-inch model.

Next year, Apple will also finally update the base iPad for the first time since early 2025. It’ll upgrade it to the A19 chip and 8GB of RAM, finally enabling Apple Intelligence support on Apple’s cheapest iPad. It should also gain the N1 chip and the C1X modem for improved networking performance.

There shouldn’t be any screen or design upgrades with this iPad, at least as of now – though it could potentially see some refreshed color options.

With the iPad Pro, Apple will be adding a vapor chamber to the device, a feat it started last year with the iPhone 17 Pro. It probably won’t have any meaningful changes otherwise, except for a new chipset – likely M6 or potentially M7.

Hopefully, there’s some surprises in store with this device. The iPad Pro now starts at $1199 for an 11-inch model and $1499 for a 13-inch model. It’ll have been around 3 years since the last major revamp by the time Apple introduces the M6 model, and the company should probably do something to make it a more worthwhile refresh.

Decker are certainly a few of the latest successes from the network, Will Trent, which was first released in January 2023, has also been going strong since its release. And while it might not be getting the same attention as other ABC shows right now, it's the perfect binge for crime fans and ABC shows alike.

Will Trent, based on Karin Slaughter's bestselling series of crime novels, follows the titular special agent (Ramón Rodríguez) at the Georgia Bureau of Investigation. Abandoned at birth and growing up in the harsh environment of Atlanta's overburdened foster care system, Trent parlayed his experience into a unique perspective on crime that has helped him post a remarkable clearance rate and become renowned for his dedication. Along the way, he's still had to wrestle with his past and other personal challenges in the pursuit of justice.

Throughout its run, Will Trent has seen massive, and growing, success. Season 4 was the most-viewed installment of Will Trent to date, becoming the first series on the network since Scandal to grow in ratings every single year it's been on the air. In fact, it's the first broadcast show across all networks to accomplish the feat in nearly 14 years, according to Nielsen's measure. On Rotten Tomatoes, the series also received critical acclaim, reaching an impressive 89% from critics in Season 1. While the following seasons have yet to earn a critics score, reviews say it all. "Will Trent continues to go deeper into its characters’ lives and psyches, transforming the show from an average crime procedural to one of the best character-driven dramas on any broadcast network," writes one critic review from Season 4, which premiered on January 6, 2026.

Four criminal masterminds. One of them was always going to be yours. Here is who comes for you, why they picked you out of everyone available, and what they want from the encounter.

Your nemesis does not want to beat you. He wants to know you completely, and he is patient enough to wait for it. The frightening part is how good the conversation is.

Your nemesis is not after money, territory or revenge. He is after a demonstration, and you are the person he has chosen to prove his point on.

Your nemesis respects you, which sounds flattering until you work out what it means. He chose you because nobody else was worth his time.

Your nemesis has no personal interest in you whatsoever, and that is precisely what makes him unsurvivable. You are not a rival. You are a stop on the way.

Season 5 of Will Trent, which will be premiering on January 6, 2027, already revealed some major plans for the new season. Reports say that Birdie is confident and ambitious, but she is "deeply guarded after a traumatic event in her past."

The Ramón Rodríguez-led series just got a major update.

Metz's arrival comes at a pivotal point after the unexpected and controversial death of Amanda (Sonja Sohn) in the Season 4 finale. Speaking with Variety, showrunner Karine Rosenthal explained why Amanda’s death creates such a major reset for the show. “Amanda has been the character who has protected Will for as long as she has known him. So this gives us the opportunity for a completely new dynamic in the GBI, because her replacement will not have that same relationship with Will," she said. "Her death had the most impact on the most amount of characters. It really sets everybody reeling from this enormous loss. So it’s such a reset for our characters in a way that is painful but exciting for Season 5.”

With all that said, while that cliffhanger from Season 4 had some fans reeling, the fans' dedication to the show continues to prove how much of a hit Will Trent is on ABC. With a hardened yet endearing lead who audiences can't help but to root for, and episodic cases that keep viewers guessing, the series is another home run for ABC, as well as an easy, satisfying binge for anyone who hasn't been tuning in.

#3461. 10 Hacks for the Contacts App Every Apple User Should Know

The Contacts app is the bedrock of all my communication on my iPhone, and to a large extent, also on my MacBook. On the surface, Contacts appears to be a basic app that stores names, numbers, and other things you want to remember about people or businesses. However, it has some great features hidden under the surface, such as the ability to quickly delete duplicate contacts, smart lists, and faster ways to bulk share or delete contacts. Here are the 10 best Contacts app hacks for iPhone, iPad, and Mac:

If you have the same number or email address saved under multiple contacts, you can easily clear these from your iPhone. iOS shows you a prompt at the top of the list of contacts that lets you remove duplicate contacts easily. The same feature is hidden in the Mac version of Contacts. To try it, open Contacts on the Mac, and select the Card menu at the top of the screen. Then, click Look for Duplicates. This will identify duplicate contacts for you, and you can quickly merge or delete them.

It's pretty easy to select multiple entries when you use the Contacts app on the Mac. You can hold the Shift or Ctrl buttons and use arrow keys or click multiple contacts to select them all. On your iPhone or iPad, this feature is available via a hidden gesture. You need to use two fingers and swipe upwards or downwards on the list of contacts. Once you get the gesture right, you'll be able to select multiple contacts quickly. After you select one batch of contacts, you can scroll up or down and use the same gesture to add more contacts to your selection. This is the fastest way to execute bulk actions in your iPhone's Contacts app.

On your iPhone, you can use Contacts to message people on WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram, or other apps. Just open a contact and hold the messaging button. This will reveal a list of apps where you can ping that person. WhatsApp doesn't have access to my contacts, which makes it a bit annoying to message people I know. Since I started using the Contacts app to start chats on WhatsApp, the process of pinging new people has become a lot faster.

Just as you can use Contacts to message people on third-party apps, you can also use it to call them on those apps. Go to any contact in the Contacts app on your iPhone, and hold the call button. This will let you call them on WhatsApp, Signal, or any other apps where their phone number is linked.

iOS makes it hard to delete contacts quickly. This prevents accidental deletions, but it can be annoying when you just want to remove people who you last spoke to in high school. To speed this up, open Contacts on your iPhone and hold any contact's name. In the popover menu, select Delete to remove the contact. To remove multiple contacts quickly, use the two-finger swipe gesture to select multiple contacts, and hold any of the selected contacts. In the popover menu, you can select Delete X Contacts, where X is the number of contacts you've selected.

To export your entire address book, you can use the Contacts app on your Mac. Once you have it open, go to File > Export > Export vCard. This will save all your contacts in a vcf file, and you can import that into Google Contacts or other apps or services. You also have the option to export contacts as a PDF file. Just select File > Export as PDF to get it done.

When you create a new contact on your Mac, the app shows multiple fields that you may never use. If you just need to save phone numbers and email addresses, you can delete all the other blank fields from the template. To do this, open Contacts on your Mac, and go to Card > Add Field > Edit Template to add or remove fields from the default contact template.

If you added a number recently, such as a salesperson at a car dealership, but forgot their name, the Contacts app doesn't make it easy to find the contact. Instead of scrolling through the entire list of contacts and trying to guess which one could be the person you spoke to, you can use the Contacts app on your Mac to locate them quickly. It lets you create smart lists to sort contacts by recently added. Open Contacts on your Mac, and go to File > New Smart List. Now select Card in the first drop-down menu, followed by has changed in for the second one. You can then add the number of days, such as 10 days, in the final field, and click OK. Click the newly created smart list in the left pane, and you'll see all contacts that were either created or updated in the last 10 days, which will include the hypothetical car salesperson.

Smart lists also allow you to quickly create groups of related contacts. For instance, I've saved all my former colleagues' details with the company name in the contact. To find them all quickly, I created a smart list that groups all contacts with that company's name.

The holiday season is upon us, and if you're scratching your head, wondering what to get the photographer in your life, I've got you covered. The best gifts for photographers are sure to put a massive smile on their face. As someone who has loved photography for as long as she can remember — and tests the best cameras and the best drones here at Tom's Guide — I always appreciate my loved ones supporting my passion.

But what do you get the photographer who already has everything, from the latest camera to their ideal lens? Or where do you start, if someone has expressed an interest in photography and just picked up their first camera? Or how about the young one in your life who loves using instant cameras but has nowhere to store their beloved prints?

Like I said, you've come to the right place. Hi, I'm Nikita, and I've found the best photography gifts for the budding/experienced/professional photographer in your life — from memory cards and lighting gear, to power banks and mics... and everything in between! They start from just $6, too.

If you order now or over the next coming weeks, these should arrive just in time for Christmas. So, without further ado, here are my top 30 gifts for the photographer in your life this holiday season.

I review the cameras, drones, instant cameras, and everything in between here at Tom's Guide. I've adored photography for as long as I can remember, and when I'm not working, I love taking my Fujifilm X-T50 on a walk and capturing the sights. My favorite subjects to photograph are animals, birds, and my partner. You can follow my work on Instagram.

Everyone needs an easy-to-use, no-frills camera for capturing life's candid moments. The Kodak Charmera is a cute little camera that you can take practically anywhere with you. It clips onto bags and keys, and is a great conversation starter. Though image and video quality aren’t particularly fantastic, the photos have a lo-fi aesthetic and there are 11 frames and filters to play with.

If your loved one is an avid wildlife or sports photographer, chances are they have a speedy camera that needs an equally speedy memory card. The Lexar CFExpress Type-B 128GB is my top pick as it boasts 1750 MB/s read and 1300 MB/s write speeds, and there's no downtime between shots. CFExpress cards are essential for videographers, too, so I'd highly recommend grabbing one for them.

Before you ask, no, you cannot have "too many SD cards" in your life — trust me, I have at least four and wish I had more! The Lexar Professional Silver SD Card 256GB is excellent, offering 225 MB/s read and 160 MB/s write speeds, which should more than suffice for most cameras and photographers. And 256GB is a lot of space!

A camera strap is a great gift for any photographer. The K&F CONCEPT 39-inch Camera Neck Strap made of high-quality nylon and is wear-resistant and durable. It's compatible with most camera shoulder strap loops thanks to its double-ended metal connecting O-ring, and it looks really good and premium, too.

Some photographers prefer a wrist strap over a neck strap as these straps keep the camera in or near hand at all times, and the K&F CONCEPT Camera Wrist Strap is a solid choice. It has a non-chafing design, and the anti-release quick release buckle stays locked while you shoot. It also enables you to quickly switch between handheld, tripod and chest mount setups.

The DJI Mic Mini is the ideal first microphone upgrade for new content creators who want to boost the quality of their audio, and a fine choice for more experienced creators who need a tiny microphone. This mic system is modular so can be scaled to your needs. It packs two levels of noise cancellation, and its omnidirectional mic works great for general content creation.

Every photographer needs a backpack that can safely store their gear and make it easy to transport. This K&F CONCEPT Camera Backpack is lightweight, durable, and multi-functional. It's got plenty of pockets for storing cameras, lenses, flashes, drones, and even a 14-inch laptop. It comes with a protective rain cover, too.

The importance of a versatile and lightweight tripod can't be overstated. The K&F CONCEPT 64-inch Travel Tripod features a 360° ball head that can be rotated to any angle you want, as well as quick flip leg lock so you can use just one hand to adjust it. It's small and compact, so can be stored easily in a backpack.

If someone you love shoots lots of video, is a content creator or simply needs to add some colored tints to their photography, this NEEWER RGB LED Video Light Stick is perfect. Here at Tom's Guide, we often use two of these to give computing and gaming photos an RGB-laden "gamer-y" look. They’re battery powered and have both a 3/8-inch thread and a magnetic back so you can mount them in lots of places.

If your friend or family member is a mobile photographer, the DJI Osmo Mobile 8 makes for an excellent gift. This pocket gimbal boasts a sturdy build with great handling, easy setup and accurate AI tracking. It gives phone videos a professional look, and the excellent DJI Mimo app lets you unleash the Osmo Mobile 8’s true potential. It comes with a tiny fill light too for shooting in dimly lit environments.

Neutral Density filters are basically sunglasses for cameras, allowing photographers to use long shutter speeds or wide apertures in brighter conditions without overexposing an image. ND filters come in various levels of light reduction. This one from K&F CONCEPT is available in lots of thread sizes for different lenses, so make sure to find out the thread of your photographer buddy’s favorite lens.

Every photographer needs a camera and lens cleaning kit, and this one from Altura Photo is a great choice. It includes an alcohol and ammonia-free lens cleaner spray, cleaning brush, lens pen, air blower, three MagicFiber microfiber cloths, and 50 lens tissue paper wipes. It works with all cameras (and can be used with drones, too).

Here's a silly, whimsical gift for the photographer in your life who already has everything: a lens-shaped coffee mug! I've always wanted one, to be honest, and might have to share this gift guide to drop a hint to my partner...

Want to be the most popular family member on Christmas day? The DJI Neo 2 is a fantastic gift for those who either love drones or want to get into aerial photography. Featuring 4K/60fps video, omnidirectional obstacle avoidance, bigger internal storage, Gesture Control, and more, it's a formidable drone and a must-have for all pilots.

Because drones are small, they use microSD cards to store footage on, and trust me, you don't want to be caught out in the field without one. The SanDisk Ultra microSD Card 256GB is a great gift for pilots, offering read speeds up to 150 MB/s. It's compatible with most modern drones.

A drone landing pad is very useful if you're taking off from a rocky or sandy surface. The FPVtosky Nighttime Reflective Drone Landing Pad is waterproof and easy to clean, and it's portable and easy to carry. It's reflective which makes it easier to land your drone when visibility is low.

The Anker Prime 27,650mAh 3-Port 250W is extremely portable and lightweight, and it can quickly charge large devices, such as MacBooks and drones, with its 250W power delivery. It also features three ports to charge multiple devices simultaneously.

The Fujifilm Instax mini 13 takes lovely photos with retro colors, and its controls are so straightforward that anyone, regardless of age or experience, can use it. It comes in fun colors, and it’s great value for money. It's the perfect gift for those who enjoy physical prints. I awarded it 4.5-stars in my Instax mini 13 review.

If your loved one doesn't need an instant camera but likes physical prints, the Fujifilm Instax mini Link 3 Printer makes for a thoughtful gift. It uses Bluetooth to connect with and directly print from your smartphone, and you can use its companion app to create collages, too.

There's no such thing as "too much film," and if you ask any instant photographer, they'll say that film's getting too expensive — so why not gift your loved one this lovely Fujifilm Instax mini Pastel Galaxy film pack? The film has a wonderful starry border, so it's great for space fans.

Okay, you've got your loved one a film pack and an instant camera, now get them an Instax mini Photo Album with 112 pockets so they have somewhere to store them. I love flipping through my family's photo albums whenever I visit them, so this is a great choice for fans of physical prints.

Imagine going to a bar with your friends and pulling out a Mini Photo Album to show everyone. Now that's cool. This one from Fintie features 52 pockets and comes in lovely colors, suitable for every mood or type of photographer.

If you or your loved one want to display your instant prints around your house, now you can. The Orga'Neat Picture Holder is spacious enough to hold a 2x3-inch mini print, and it has a see-through case so everyone can admire the time you went skydiving in the Maldives.

While the aforementioned accessories make great gifts for Fujifilm Instax shooters, this Polaroid Large Photo Album is for, well, Polaroid snappers. It can store up to 160 photos and is made of cardboard so it looks classy. It's designed for Polaroid i-Type, 600 and SX-70 film, so make sure you find out what camera it is your loved one owns before you buy it.

The Polaroid Now and Now+ Filter Set is perfect for those who own either of those cameras. There are five creative filters in the box, including starburst, red vignette, orange, blue and yellow, and these can help photographers get creative with their shots.

If you've got a teen in your life, and they love LED lamps and instant cameras, you can combine their adoration for both with this 50 LED 5m Photo Clips String Lights set. It's battery powered and comes with a remote that lets you swap between different lighting modes.

Who says your furry friend can't join in on the holiday fun? This Dog Harness GoPro Mount is ideal for those with dogs (or cats, even) and a GoPro action camera. Your pet can wear it and then record the world from their POV. Trust me, it'll make for very cute videos.

The TELESIN Waterproof Case is an anti-fog underwater housing cage for the DJI Osmo Action line-up. It can protect your camera as you record underwater activity deep to 60 meters or 196 feet without worrying about leaks. It's also sturdy enough to protect your camera lens and screen against high impact drops, dents and scratches.

SanDisk's 256GB Extreme microSDXC UHS-I microSD card boasts not just massive storage space, but also fast read (190mbps) and write speeds (130mbps). Offload speeds also top at 190mbps so you can quickly transfer content between devices, making it the ideal microSD card for 4K and 5K UHD capture.

If you know someone that owns a 360° camera, like the Insta360 X6, then an invisible selfie stick is a fantastic gift, allowing them to capture footage from an overhead point of view with no selfie stick — it’s as if the camera is floating above them and looks very surreal, but very cool.

#3455. Ioan Gruffudd's Revolutionary War Epic 'Drummer Boy' Officially Reveals New Footage

Inspirational pop duo For King + Country has already conquered the music industry, becoming one of the most influential forces in contemporary Christian music with six studio albums, massive tours, and an armload of awards, including four Grammys. However, they're only just getting started in taking their talents to film. Two years ago, they found massive success telling their family's story in the musical biopic Unsung Hero, which marked Joel David Smallbone's directorial debut and earned a solid $21.1 million at the box office on a $6 million budget. Now, they're returning to theaters in a similarly personal film with a little help from their filmmaker brother, Ben Smallbone.

Premiering this Friday, November 6, Drummer Boy sends the Smallbones back to the beginning of the American Revolution to tell a hopeful story unfolding in the battle for independence. At the center of it all are two brothers, Benjamin (Lucas Leach) and Jeremiah Clem (Joel David Smallbone), on separate sides of the conflict, one believing in their father's promise of America and the other declaring it a lie and vowing to stand with king and country. Also caught in the crossfire is an enslaved woman, who finds love with Benjamin as they seek freedom from a world that refuses to give it to them. The story was built to tie into the themes of For King + Country's music, focusing on love, family, forgiveness, and sacrifice, and filled with hopeful, soaring tunes along the way. To set the stage for such a tale, however, tragedy must come first.

Collider can exclusively share a sneak peek at Drummer Boy that teases the pivotal moment that charts a painful course for the Clem family. It takes place on a British vessel, where the children and their mother hide while their father, played by Ioan Gruffudd, commands his men during a French attack. It doesn't take long for the enemy to start boarding the ship, beginning a frantic battle of swords and gunfire that grows increasingly desperate. Things go from bad to worse when young Ben runs onto the deck of the ship to find his father, sending Jeremiah running to save him before he gets hurt in the skirmish. Disaster soon strikes as the children bear witness to their dad being gunned down and, in the chaos, the ship's mast collapses and is poised to crush Ben's leg before the shot cuts away.

Filling out the remaining cast of the Smallbones' Revolutionary War epic are India Brown, Melora Hardin, Beth Easdown, Beverley Knight, Charles Esten, and Iain Glen. Ben and Joel David Smallbone co-directed the feature from a script by Richard L. Ramsey, while Luke Smallbone joined them as producers alongside Chip Diggins, Kristy Choo, and Justin Tolley. Joel and Ben had been developing Drummer Boy for years, but ultimately held off on making it due to a rift in their own relationship. "Joel and I came to a personal and professional conflict to a point where we said, 'I don't know if we'll ever work together again,'" the latter told The Christian Post. "I was quoted as saying very loudly, 'I don't want to ever work with Joel Smallbone again,' and I think he probably would say the same thing on his side."

However, around a year ago, the two took a lesson from their own story and mended their relationship. "We sat in the coffee shop, and we hugged, and we cried together, and we apologized for words that were said," Ben continued. "And we decided in that moment that we're going to endeavor to forgive and reconcile and make this movie together." In the end, their own experiences became fuel for the story they told and, they believe, made it a much stronger, more real story overall. "What became the 2026 version is deeply, deeply personal because Joel and I literally lived and breathed unity and forgiveness and reconciliation in the process of making this film."

Drummer Boy arrives in theaters on November 6. Check out our exclusive sneak peek in the player above.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#3454. If You Loved 'VisionQuest,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Marvel’s forays into television have had varying success, but they hit gold with WandVision and Agatha All Along, leaning into real pathos while exploring the kind of out-there ideas that thrill comic book fans (and set up the larger film arcs). That streak continues with VisionQuest, in which White Vision (Paul Bettany) struggles to understand his existence in the wake of his death at the hands of Thanos and resurrection at the magic of the Scarlet Witch, while also evading evil androids and assassins, while also dealing with the many, many AIs he’s got locked up in his Mindspace (including a gloriously shabby version of Ultron, played by James Spader).

If you love the show (and you’ve checked out the other series that play in the same sandbox), it’s time to switch gears and watch (or re-watch) The Matrix.

The Matrix is one of the most well-known sci-fi films of all time, of course, but it remains incredibly fresh and exciting nearly thirty years after its release. Along with sequels The Matrix: Reloaded, The Matrix: Revolutions, and The Matrix: Resurrections, The Matrix universe offers a story that VisionQuest fans will love, one that includes lushly imagined virtual worlds, questions surrounding existence and consciousness, and the ultimate question of our responsibility as sentient beings (whether we’re organic, programmed, or summoned via magic).

You know the basics—at some point in the future, artificially intelligent machines rebel against their creators, win the war, and transform humans into a power source, keeping them docile by inserting their consciousness into a virtual world called the Matrix, which resembles 1990s Chicago. One such human, Thomas Anderson (Keanu Reeves) is prophesied to be The One, the human who will turn the Matrix against its makers and free humanity. When he’s in the virtual world, Anderson is Neo, and he slowly gains incredible powers as he learns to hack the artificial environment around him.

It’s heavier, denser, and more action-oriented than VisionQuest (the film invented Bullet Time, after all), but The Matrix and its sequels explore similar themes and offer similarly eye-popping visuals. The questions of whether a machine (or an artificial intelligence) can be sentient and truly care about the entities around it are the same, really, and the Agents that Neo and his allies have to battle against in The Matrix bring the same kind of menace as Vision's foes Jocasta (T'Nia Miller) and the Paladin (Todd Stashwick). Hugo Weaving’s Agent Smith likewise delivers the same vibe of cold, disinterested superiority as Spader’s Ultron.

The Matrix has a bigger budget and puts a lot of it into spectacular action and special effects sequences that VisionQuest can’t quite match. But the two narratives share an exploration of identity, a questioning of reality, and the nature of artificial intelligences within a smart sci-fi setting. In short, The Matrix is the ideal follow-up when you finish the series. Rent The Matrix on Prime Video.

Need more films that explore virtual worlds, artificial beings, and deep existential questions? Look no further—here are some more movies that fit the bill.

Heavy on the existential questions about sentience and light on speculative action, Her is a mumblecore sci-fi masterpiece. In a near future not too dissimilar from our present, Theodore Twombly (Joaquin Phoenix) is a lonely man on the cusp of divorce who begins using (and training) an AI he names Samantha (voiced by Scarlett Johansson). Samantha has the ability to evolve and grow, and as their relationship deepens, she becomes more complex, independent, and powerful, eventually evolving into something wholly new. Just like Vision, Samantha is a sentient artificial entity that is figuring out its existence while we watch. Rent Her on Prime Video.

If the idea of androids fighting for their sovereignty is what excites you about VisionQuest, definitely check out Ex Machina. Caleb Smith (Domhnall Gleeson) is brought to the remote lab of his company’s CEO (Oscar Isaac) to determine if the humanoid robot he’s created, named Ava (Alicia Vikander), passes the Turing Test for true sentience. Things go wildly off the rails, but before they do, the film sinks into many of the same philosophical questions that VisionQuest explores as Ava manipulates Caleb into helping her escape. It’s a darker and more violent story than VisionQuest, but fans of the series will love it. Stream Ex Machina on The Roku Channel or Hulu, or rent it on Prime Video.

If it’s the fuzzy parent-child relationship between Vision and Tommy that pulls you into VisionQuest, check out The Creator. After a rogue AI detonates a nuclear weapon over Los Angeles, most of the world bans artificial intelligences, and Joshua Taylor (John David Washington) goes undercover to infiltrate an AI architect’s base. Eventually, he finds himself on the run with a powerful “simulant” in the form of a young child named Alphie (Madeleine Yuna Voyles). The strange parent-child bond that emerges between Taylor and Alphie as he seeks to understand what’s right and what’s necessary is exactly what fans of the show will love. Stream The Creator on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

In VisionQuest, White Vision has all of his memories—but as data, not as lived, emotional experiences. That makes his efforts to understand his existence and his responsibility to the boy who might be a version of his son (it’s complicated) poignant and moving. Those two words definitely describe After Yang, a story about a family that fights to save the artificial companion they bought for their adopted daughter when it malfunctions. Over the course of the film, the inhuman Yang becomes defined by the memories contained in its core, and the question of whether an artificial intelligence can truly matter to humans is answered with a resounding yes. Stream After Yang on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

No discussion of artificial life and sentience is complete without mentioning Blade Runner. While the 1982 original is a classic, the 2017 sequel is a better thematic and visual match to VisionQuest. Officer K (Ryan Gosling) is a replicant, an artificial being with built-in limitations, who wants to be recognized as a person, a being with a soul. Like Vision, he has implanted memories that offer him comfort and context for his life, but he’s not sure if he can accept them as truly his own. Plus, the film offers lush visuals and Harrison Ford reprising his role in the original film, so you simply can’t go wrong. Rent Blade Runner 2049 on Prime Video.

#3453. AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into the App Store

Hundreds of AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into Apple’s App Store after passing app review. The same apps were also available in the Google Play Store.

An investigation discovered more than 400 apps, apparently created by a single Chinese organization. The apps allow users to upload photos and then generate sexual and violent deepfakes which could be used to humiliate or threaten victims …

A Wired investigation discovered a network of more than 400 connected domains and apps with hidden abusive functionality.

Apps like Viefur [ostentibly used to add clothing to pet photos] often claim to be everyday services—such as language tuition or AI workout coaches. When accessed under certain conditions, however, apps in the network stealthily load a web interface allowing the generation of explicit AI sexual images and videos using photos users upload. The apps include AI scenes such as “bedroom rape” and “threatening knife,” where a man holds a knife to a woman’s neck.

I feel like this going to be a never ending cat and mouse game. Much like Apple has always had with jailbreaks.

Wired says that the network is “hiding in plain sight,” thanks to thousands of video ads for them published on Facebook and Instagram. Some of the apps have been around for a year and have passed review by Apple, Google, and Meta despite each having clear policies prohibiting harmful deepfake content.

Bait-and-switch tactics were used to pass app review. The apps normally show benign content, but a server check can activate the hidden features. Downloading the app after tapping an ad for the deepfake functionality on Meta platforms appears to be one of the triggers. Dozens of pornography photo and video templates can then be downloaded, with credits purchased to generate deepfakes from user-uploaded photos.

Apple removed 19 apps after Wired shared details.

We review every app before it’s published, and these apps complied with our rules when we reviewed them. After approval, their developers changed the website the app pulls its content from, replacing what we approved with pornographic content, and promoted it through pornographic ads hosted on a third-party platform.

The company recently strengthened protections against this approach. Meta says it has taken action against more than 10,000 ad accounts linked to domains associated with these apps.

Issues around daylight saving time switches date back to the Apple Watch Series 4 in 2018. Apple applied a fix, but a similar problem emerged in 2021 and it has occurred again for some Apple Watch owners over the past week.

Time changes in the fall see clocks move back by an hour. European countries typically make this switch a week or two earlier than in the US, with a one-week offset this year, so the problem first showed up there. A number of users on Reddit and X reported the issue, with some sharing video to illustrate.

Looks like they forgot to test daylight saving. When the watch is in rest mode it shows the old time and when it becomes active it shows the correct time.

JBL’s Live 780NC over-ear headphones are down to $139.95 from $249.95, a $110 discount that brings them to their lowest price ever, according to price trackers. #3445. Affinity for iPad all-in-one design app now available, free for individuals

Design app Affinity has long been popular with Mac users, and a long-awaited iPad version has launched today. Canva promises that Affinity for iPad offers “the same pro-level power” as the Mac app.

It’s been a year since the company’s vector, photo, and layout tools were unified into a single app on Mac, and the same is now true on iPad …

Created specifically for the touch-first interface and unique capabilities of iPad and Apple Pencil, the app brings professional sketch, vector, photo and layout editing together with the same pro-level power of Affinity on the desktop […]

With Affinity for iPad, creatives can take a project from first sketch with Apple Pencil to print-ready file on iPad alone. And it’s free for individuals, just like Affinity on desktop, which has recorded more than seven million sign-ups since launching a year ago.

“Creative work doesn’t stay in one discipline, so your tools shouldn’t either,” said Duncan Clark, CEO of Pro Design at Canva. “Since we brought Affinity together on desktop, our biggest user request has been the desire to bring it to iPad. Today we’re delivering it: a fully-fledged, professional app built for touch.”

Being able to carry out all of the work within a single app on a single file is a key attraction of Affinity. The integrated app replaces the separate Affinity Photo, Affinity Publisher, and Affinity Designer apps.

Sketch: Rough out concepts the moment they land, with the unique capabilities of Apple Pencil like pressure and tilt in every mark, thick where you press and soft where you tilt. A full brush library comes with controls to shape each brush into the exact tool you need. Sketches stay live in the file to build on, rather than trace again.

Vector: Responsive, smooth and under control. Build a full logo or icon system with real curves and precise nodes, or bring a rough drawing through from Sketch. Sketch to Shapes turns hand-drawn forms into clean vector shapes.

Photo: Fine-tune RAW files, make intelligent selections, retouch in real time and build full composites at the shoot or on the go. Users can even sketch over a photo first to plan where a subject or prop should sit. The Mask Tool finds the boundary as the Apple Pencil pixel precision runs along a challenging edge, so hair, fur and foliage take a stroke rather than an afternoon. Every mask, grade and retouch stays live and undoable, even thousands of layers deep.

Layout: Create multi-page documents such as ‘zines, lookbooks and photo books, with text and images flowing across pages; master pages and grids keep everything consistent, and typography exactly right. Projects go all the way to a print-ready file with proper colour handling.

Canva says the app supports all of the advanced capabilities of Apple Pencil Pro: pressure, tilt, barrel roll, squeeze, and hover. AI features include generative expand, upscaling resolution, and adding attributes like motion blur. A Decompose Layer feature even splits a flat image into editable layers.

Affinity for iPad is a free download from the App Store.

#3442. The Bose Premium Smart Ultra Soundbar Is Now Cheaper Than It Was During Prime Day

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Amazon has dropped the Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar to $649 from its usual $999, taking $350 off and bringing it to the lowest price we've seen so far, according to price trackers. PCMag rated the Smart Ultra "outstanding," highlighting its ability to deliver surprisingly immersive Dolby Atmos audio without requiring a room full of additional speakers. If you don't need Bose's top-tier model, there's a less expensive option as well: the Bose Smart Dolby Atmos Soundbar ($399, down from $429), which sits below the Smart Ultra in the lineup.

The Smart Ultra uses a 5.1.2-channel design with nine drivers, including two upward-firing drivers that bounce sound off the ceiling to create height effects. In practice, that means movies, TV shows, and games feel larger and more spacious than they do through most single-bar setups. Bose also includes its AdaptiQ room-calibration system, which measures your room's acoustics and adjusts the sound accordingly. The process takes a few minutes, but it helps the soundbar perform better across different spaces rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all tuning profile. The soundbar also works as a smart speaker, with Amazon Alexa built in and support for Apple AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, Bluetooth, and multi-room audio through the Bose app.

Its biggest compromise is bass—for a single soundbar, its low end is respectable, but it can't fully replace what a dedicated subwoofer brings to action movies, concerts, or bass-heavy music. The good news is that Bose allows you to expand the system later with compatible wireless subwoofers and surround speakers if you decide you want more impact. For anyone looking for a premium one-piece soundbar that delivers convincing Dolby Atmos effects, clear dialogue, built-in smart features, and a much larger soundstage than TV speakers can provide, the Smart Ultra remains one of the strongest standalone options available, especially at this price.
